# Train Like a Warrior, Rest Like a Son
## Scripture
"Have you not known? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He does not faint or grow weary; his understanding is unsearchable. He gives power to the faint, and to him who has no might he increases strength." – Isaiah 40:28–29
## Reflection
Men love the image of the warrior—the one who pushes through, never quits, carries the weight. And there's truth there. But Isaiah gives us a harder, holier lesson: even the strongest young men "faint and grow weary" (v. 30). Your willpower has a ceiling. Your body will fail. Pretending otherwise isn't faith—it's pride.

The warrior who lasts is the one who knows where strength actually comes from. God doesn't merely top off your tank; He gives power to the faint and increases strength to the one who has none. That means your weakness is not disqualifying—it's the doorway. When you hit the wall in the gym, in your marriage, in your walk with God, you're not failing the test. You're being invited to stop white-knuckling and start trusting.

Real discipline isn't self-reliance dressed in gym clothes. It's showing up, doing the work, and humbly receiving the strength God supplies. Train hard. But rest in the One who never grows weary.
## Daily Challenge
Before your workout today, pause for 30 seconds and ask God for strength—then give Him the effort. Do 25 pushups, and on each rep thank Him that His strength is made perfect in your weakness.
